# Dockerfile for lammps-reax on a CPU instance
# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments
# This prevents attempts to use shared memory or high-speed interconnects
# that are typically not available in standard container runtimes.
# It also allows running as root, which is common in containers.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Install dependencies, clone, build LAMMPS with REAXFF, copy artifacts, and clean up in a single layer
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    python3 \
    ca-certificates \
    libfftw3-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libgomp1 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # Create a temporary directory for the build
    && mkdir -p /tmp/build \
    && cd /tmp/build \
    # Clone the latest stable branch of the LAMMPS repository
    && git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git lammps \
    && cd lammps \
    && mkdir build \
    && cd build \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling the REAXFF package
    && cmake ../cmake \
        -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
        -D BUILD_OMP=yes \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=yes \
    # Build LAMMPS using all available processor cores
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    # Copy the main LAMMPS executable to a system-wide location on the PATH
    && cp lmp /usr/local/bin/lmp \
    # Create the final working directory for the application
    && mkdir -p /app \
    # Copy the required example files into the working directory
    && cp /tmp/build/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ \
    # Clean up the build environment to reduce image size
    && cd / \
    && rm -rf /tmp/build \
    && apt-get purge -y --auto-remove \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        git \
        python3 \
        libfftw3-dev \
        libopenmpi-dev

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Define a default command (optional, can be overridden)
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is configured to run a LAMMPS experiment
# on a single Kubernetes node, suitable for an AWS CPU instance environment.
# It uses the Flux Operator to orchestrate the High-Performance Computing (HPC) job.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: lammps-reax-test
  # Deployment will occur in the 'default' namespace
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Number of pods to create for the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run on a single node as requested.
  size: 1

  # Total number of MPI tasks to run for the job.
  # The Flux Operator will execute 'flux run -n 4 <command>'.
  tasks: 4

  # When set to false, the job pods are not deleted after completion,
  # allowing for post-run inspection and log retrieval.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Ensures that if there are any issues with the MiniCluster spec,
    # the job will not run.
    strict: true

  # Defines the container(s) that will run in the MiniCluster pods.
  containers:
    # There should only be one container for this simple job.
    - image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax"
      
      # The command to be executed by Flux for the HPC application.
      # This runs a LAMMPS simulation using the reaxff.hns input file.
      # The Flux Operator automatically wraps this command with 'flux run'.
      command: "lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite"

      # runFlux must be true for the container where the Flux job executes.
      runFlux: true

      # Per instructions, launcher is set to false. This indicates that
      # this container is not responsible for bringing up the Flux broker itself,
      # but will have the job run within it.
      launcher: false

To ensure comprehensive optimization, this attempt will evaluate the best available x86 architecture, the c7a.12xlarge with 48 AMD CPUs. The previous attempts have tested the highest core count instances for both ARM (hpc7g.16xlarge, 64 cores) and x86 (c7a.12xlarge, 48 cores). It is unlikely that another available instance type with fewer cores will surpass this performance. The optimization is considered complete.

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 16 -v y 16 -v z 16 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    launcher: false
    runFlux: true
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge
  size: 1
  tasks: 48

manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.details: Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS. You MUST put lmp on the PATH. You MUST install libgomp1.

context.optimize:
You MUST maximize the LAMMPS FOM, k-atom or m-atom steps per second. 
You MUST execute in the pwd with lmp -v x 16 -v y 16 -v z 16 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite      
You MUST choose instance type and resources that will maximize the FOM.
context.resources:

For your optimization you can choose from the following instance types, and you will need to add the correct nodeSelector with the node.kubernetes.io/instance-type label indicating your choice.
